model-agency.lead: OpenUP model agency in Moscow. The site already ran on Tilda but looked dated and responded sluggishly. We redesigned the home page, header and footer, cleaned up the model catalogues and made the site bilingual.

facts.v: Refresh the site and open it to an English-speaking audience
Redesign and hand-written markup on top of Tilda
Home page, header, footer, catalogues, ru/en translation

blocks.title: The starting point
paragraphs: The agency's site ran on Tilda but looked dated: the styling lagged behind how model agencies present themselves today, and some of the content had not been updated in a long time.
The interface was slow to respond, and the navigation followed old patterns and no longer fit every section — and the agency has many: women, men, arrivals, new faces, international, production.

blocks.title: What we built
paragraphs: We designed a new home page, header and footer, then built them ourselves — not assembled from ready-made blocks, but written as markup and styles by hand on top of the builder.

The header gained a multi-level menu with dropdown sections, the mobile version a burger panel with social links, and on small screens the footer collapses its sections into an accordion. None of this comes with Tilda out of the box.

blocks.title: Model catalogues
paragraphs: The catalogues run on Tilda Store, and the default card layout did not suit the agency: a model roster is a showcase, not a product list.
We changed the display format, the card corner radii and their placement on the page, then went through the breakpoints separately so the grid holds on any screen.

blocks.title: Bilingual without a second site
paragraphs: Tilda offers no real bilingual support: the usual route is duplicating every page and then maintaining two copies of the site. Instead we wrote a script that translates the page on the fly when the ru or en button is clicked.

It carries its own dictionary of more than 800 pairs; strings missing from it are fetched from external translators with a fallback and then cached. Catalogue search is solved separately: model names are stored in Latin script, so a Russian query is rewritten inside the request to the server — visitors search in Russian and find what they need.

blocks.title: The outcome
paragraphs: Everything visible was refreshed: the home page, header, footer and catalogues. The navigation now fits every section of the agency, including the link to its children's branch.

The English version runs without a second site and without duplicate pages — there is one set of pages and one dictionary to maintain, and that dictionary is edited in a Google Sheet without touching code. The client does not share business metrics, so the numbers here are about our work only: everything described can be checked by opening the site.

skynia-hall.lead: SKYNIA HALL is an event venue next to Volgogradsky Prospekt metro: a main hall for 1,200 guests, a small hall and six meeting rooms. The old site showed the hall as one long page and didn't answer the key question — will it work for my wedding, conference or prom? facts.v: A site that sells the hall for a specific event and collects requests
Redesign and custom code blocks inside Tilda
Home page, 12 format pages, booking, legal pages

metrics.label: from choosing a hall to a request

blocks.title: The starting point
paragraphs: The venue had a draft of a new site and a clear feeling: it should look premium, not templated. The old Tilda page showed the hall, but guests had to call to find out whether their event would fit, what it cost and whether the date was free.
Booking lived on a separate page and requests had to be clarified by phone — a long way for someone who just wanted to ask about Saturday.

blocks.title: Design in three rounds
paragraphs: The first, light version felt too plain. The second — a serif and gold — was beautiful but hard to read. The third kept the dark background and gold accent but switched to Geologica and Golos Text: premium and easy to read on a phone.

We removed extra labels, left the first screen with a headline, one line and two buttons, and gave every section a clear next step. On desktop a short “Check available dates” form sits next to the hero.

blocks.title: Three-step booking
paragraphs: The separate booking page became a three-step window: hall and format, date and guests, contacts. A preliminary total is shown right away, the draft is saved if the guest gets distracted, and the selection can be sent to WhatsApp with one button.
On phones a smart bar sits at the bottom: its button label changes by section — “Book the hall”, “Pick a format”, “Ask a question” — and a round button opens call, WhatsApp and Telegram.

blocks.title: 12 pages for event formats
paragraphs: Wedding, corporate party, conference, prom, concert, training, exhibition and five more formats got their own pages: a headline for the search query, fitting photos, real events from the venue, answers to common questions and a form that already knows which event it's about.
Each page has its own meta tags, Schema.org markup and social cover, and they all share one frame: a new landing page is assembled from ready blocks rather than built from scratch.

blocks.title: Our own code inside Tilda
paragraphs: The venue wanted to stay on Tilda and edit texts and photos itself. So the design is built from custom blocks with our code: the editor works as usual and the layout holds on every screen.
The header, footer and booking window are shared across the site. Requests from every form land in Tilda CRM marked with the page and form they came from.

blocks.title: Speed, search and legal pages
paragraphs: Photos are served as WebP through Tilda's CDN, fonts are uploaded to the platform and unused code is stripped at build time: the mobile version scores 97 of 100 for performance in Lighthouse and 100 for accessibility, SEO and best practices.
We added a personal data policy, a separate consent document and a short cookie notice; Yandex Metrica starts only after it.

blocks.title: The outcome
paragraphs: The site now leads a guest from the event format to a request instead of just showing the hall. The venue updates texts, photos and prices itself, and new pages are built from the same block system.
The new version is being prepared to move to the main domain — we'll add a link to the live site after launch.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: We respect your privacy. Below is what personal data the site collects, why it is needed and how you can manage it.

sections.heading: 1. General provisions
paragraphs: This Policy governs how personal data of visitors to the sandwor website (the “Site”) is processed and protected, and is prepared in accordance with Russian Federal Law No. 152-FZ of 27 July 2006 “On Personal Data”.
The data operator is Alexander Olegovich Vorobyov (the “Operator”). Contact for personal-data matters: aovorobyov@mail.ru.
By using the Site and submitting data through its forms, you confirm your agreement with this Policy.

sections.heading: 2. What data is processed
paragraphs: When you fill in the forms on the Site, the Operator processes the data you provide voluntarily: name, email address, phone number, Telegram username, and the text of your message or task description.

When you visit the Site, technical data is processed automatically: IP address, cookies, browser and device information, and on-page activity. It is collected via the Yandex.Metrica web-analytics service.

sections.heading: 3. Purposes of processing
paragraphs: Personal data is processed in order to: handle requests submitted through the forms; contact you upon your request; and improve the Site and analyse its traffic.

sections.heading: 4. Legal basis
paragraphs: The basis for processing is the consent of the data subject. You give it by ticking the relevant checkbox when submitting a form or by continuing to use the Site with analytics enabled. Consent may be withdrawn at any time (see the section on rights).

sections.heading: 5. Manner and means of processing
paragraphs: Processing is carried out both with and without automation. Data submitted through the forms reaches the Operator as a message in the Telegram messenger and is used solely to contact you.
The Operator does not sell personal data and does not transfer it to third parties, except as described in this Policy or required by law.

sections.heading: 6. Cookies and web analytics
paragraphs: The Site uses cookies and the Yandex.Metrica service (Yandex LLC, servers located in the Russian Federation) to analyse traffic. Metrica may collect your IP address, cookies, device data and on-site behaviour.

Analytics loads only after your consent in the cookie banner; if you decline, the counter is not loaded. You can withdraw consent by clearing site data in your browser or disabling cookies in its settings.

sections.heading: 7. Retention periods
paragraphs: Personal data is kept no longer than the purposes of processing require, or until consent is withdrawn. Once the purposes are achieved or consent is withdrawn, the data is deleted unless the law provides otherwise.

sections.heading: 8. Data protection
paragraphs: The Operator takes reasonable organisational and technical measures to protect personal data from unlawful access, alteration, disclosure and destruction.

sections.heading: 9. Rights of the data subject
paragraphs: You have the right to obtain information about the processing of your data, to request its correction, blocking or deletion, and to withdraw your consent. To exercise these rights, send a request to aovorobyov@mail.ru.

sections.heading: 10. Withdrawal of consent
paragraphs: You can withdraw consent to the processing of personal data by emailing aovorobyov@mail.ru. After withdrawal, the Operator stops processing and deletes the data unless there is another lawful basis to retain it.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to this Policy
paragraphs: The Operator may amend this Policy. The current version is always published on this page.

sections.heading: 12. Contacts
paragraphs: For any questions related to the processing of personal data, contact aovorobyov@mail.ru.
